hook: Most professional fund managers lose to an investment so boring it barely tries.
on_screen_hook: The boring fund that *beats* most pros

blocks.narration: Most professional fund managers lose to an investment so boring it barely tries. It is called an index fund.
blocks.visual: A clay race track where flashy race cars sputter while a slow, steady clay tortoise crosses the finish line

blocks.narration: An index fund simply buys every company in a list. An S and P five hundred fund owns roughly five hundred large American companies.
blocks.visual: A single clay basket fills with hundreds of tiny building-shaped tokens, each a different company

blocks.narration: There is no genius picking winners. The fund just follows the list, so its trading and costs stay low.
blocks.visual: A tiny robot calmly follows a printed checklist while busy suited figures run around in the background

blocks.narration: Active funds try to beat the market by picking stocks. That takes research teams, frequent trading, and higher fees.
blocks.visual: Clay figures in suits shout at screens, papers flying, coins leaking from their pockets

blocks.narration: S and P's long-running scorecards have found most actively managed large company funds trail the index over long stretches like fifteen years.
blocks.visual: A long timeline where most of the flashy cars fall behind the tortoise one by one

blocks.narration: Part of the reason is math. Before fees, investors as a group earn the market return. After fees, the average active investor earns less.
blocks.visual: A pie split evenly among figures, then small slices taken back by a hand labeled with a percent symbol

blocks.narration: Index funds will never beat the market. That is the point. They aim to match it, cheaply, for decades.
blocks.visual: The tortoise steadily climbs a gentle hill that rises toward a sunrise

blocks.narration: Boring can be a feature. Follow for the next one, where we break down what an expense ratio really costs you.
blocks.visual: The tortoise rests on a pile of gold coins as the camera pulls back

captions.hook_line: Most professional fund managers lose to this boring investment 🤯
captions.body: An S&P 500 index fund owns roughly 500 large US companies in one purchase. S&P's SPIVA scorecards have found most actively managed large-cap funds trail the index over long periods.

youtube_title: Index Funds: The Boring Investment That Beats Most Pros
